Subject: Infrastructure governance questions & topology deliverable

Hi Liam / MedAlign security team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we stay aligned on requirements: 

What we covered
- SOC 2: you mentioned an upcoming Type II audit in Q4 and existing Type I reports; we requested the scope (in-scope systems) and any exception notes.
- Data residency & GDPR: geography of tenant data, cross-border replication allowed?
- HIPAA: confirmation that MedAlign requires BAA and details on PHI flows.
- Network isolation: options discussed — VPC with private subnets + strict egress, and an air-gapped on-prem option for high-risk workloads.
- Evidence & artifacts: infrastructure diagram, list of controls, sample syslog retention policy, vendor questionnaire (we'll kick this off).

Deliverables we propose from Redwood
1) Initial topology sketch (VPC + private-only egress) — due 2026-10-27
2) Completed vendor security questionnaire (first pass) — due 2026-10-29
3) Short write-up on BAA/KMS integration for HIPAA workloads — due 2026-11-03

Please confirm the scope items you expect in the topology sketch (e.g., bastions, NAT, private endpoints, VPC endpoints for cloud storage, HSM/KMS placement). I attached an initial RFI workbook we started during the call (initial-rfi.xlsx).

If that timeline looks okay, we'll also schedule a 30-minute follow-up on 2026-10-28 to walk the sketch and answer any technical specifics.

Thanks,
Sofia

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Infrastructure governance questions & topology deliverable

Sofia —

Thanks for the summary and the RFI workbook. A few clarifications from our side before you finalize the topology: 

- SOC 2: Correct — we completed Type I in 2025 and have a Type II audit in November 2026. In-scope systems include our patient platform and API gateway; the infrastructure layer is partially in-scope. We'll share the auditor contact and a redacted report after a short internal review.
- HIPAA / BAA: yes, we require a signed BAA for any environment that stores or processes PHI. For sketches, please annotate where PHI might flow (e.g., temporary KV cache, object storage).
- KMS: We prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) in HSM-backed KMS for production; for the initial topology sketch, indicate both CMK and Redwood-managed key options.
- Air-gap: For highly sensitive workloads we want an option that can be deployed behind a physical air-gap. That option can be an appendix to the main sketch — include a short list of what that would change (no egress, offline updates, offline logging collection).

Attachments: I've uploaded a short site security overview (site-security-overview.pdf) and our procurement timeline. We'll aim to provide the auditor contact by EOD Friday.

Appreciate the timeline — the VPC sketch by 10/27 is critical for our architecture review committee.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
IT Director, MedAlign Health
it-director@medalign.com | +1 (646) 555-4412

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Infrastructure governance questions & topology deliverable

Looping in a quick technical note that I'll include in the sketch: 

- Option A (Hosted VPC, recommended starter): single-tenant VPC per environment, private subnets for inference nodes, private NAT for egress with proxy allowlist, VPC endpoints for storage (no public internet to model data stores). KMS: show both customer-managed CMK in HSM (preferred) and Redwood-managed key.
- Option B (Dedicated with strict segmentation): dedicated GPU pool in isolated subnets, separate logging path to a customer-delegated logging bucket, SIEM ingest via secure egress-to-SIEM endpoint.
- Appendix (Air-gapped): physical separation, patching via signed bundles, local logging collector with periodic offline export. Note: this path increases operational overhead and SLA delta; we'll list tradeoffs.

I'll attach a quick draft of the segmentation diagram (vpc-segmentation-options.svg) and a checklist of artifacts we'll provide: architecture diagram, control mapping to SOC 2 categories, encryption key flow, retention policy example, and a completed vendor questionnaire.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Solutions — Redwood Inference
